title: Earth’s inner core is about as hot as the surface of the Sun
body: More than 5,000 km beneath your feet sits a ball of iron and nickel nearly 2,500 km across, with an estimated temperature around 5,400 °C, similar to the Sun’s surface. At that heat it should melt, but pressure of roughly 3.3 to 3.6 million atmospheres keeps it solid. No one has ever sampled it: Danish seismologist Inge Lehmann discovered it in 1936 by studying how earthquake waves travel through the planet.

slides.question: The inner core is hot enough to melt, so why is it solid?
options: The outer core cools it down
It is really a very dense gas
slides.explanation: Pressure of roughly 3.3 to 3.6 million atmospheres keeps the iron and nickel solid at around 5,400 °C. Inge Lehmann found the core in 1936 by studying earthquake waves.
